name: Apollo Tyres
why: Record quarterly sales, annual sales, annual profit
Credit rating AA+/Stable (CRISIL) - strong balance sheet
Domestic institutions (mutual funds, insurers) raised holding by 5.4 pts in a year
Profits backed by cash: operating cash flow is 212% of 3-year profit
risks: Margins shrinking (15% to 11%) - record profit may be near peak
Working capital stretching - debtor days 43 to 41, inventory days 127 to 128 (rising): check receivables / stock build-up
FIIs (foreign funds) cut holding by 1.8 pts in a year
Cost quality weak: margin shrinking or operating profit falling (costs 85% to 89% of sales)
Sector cycle: Weak / out of favour

capex: As on 30th September 2026, consolidated net debt to EBITDA stood at just 0.9 times, providing substantial capacity to fund future growth while maintaining a prudent capital structure.
risks: Coming to the performance, the second quarter was characterized by a challenging operating environment, marked by persistent geopolitical uncertainty and significant inflation in the key raw material cost.
Despite these headwinds, I am very happy to say that the busy delivered a resilient performance and continued to execute on its strategic priorities.
focus: Equally importantly, we remain focused on strengthening organizational capability.
And in the first two quarters, there is a massive focus on getting the whole supply chain in place.

about: Apollo, established in 1972, manufactures automatic bias and radial tyres, and tubes. It has plants in Kochi, Vadodara, Pune, and Chennai. The product profile includes prominent tyre brands in the T&B, light truck, passenger car, and farm vehicle segments in India, catering to both original equipment manufacturers, and the replacement market.
